title.narrative: Emergency Response to Flood-Affected Communities in Adamawa State, Nigeria

description.narrative: On the 27th July 2025, communities in the Yola area of the Adamawa state experienced severe flooding which has displaced an estimated 10,000 people across Fufore, Yola South, and Demsa LGAs in Adamawa State. Dozens were injured, and thousands were displaced after heavy rains triggered flash flooding across multiple communities. The flash flooding submerged homes, destroyed infrastructure, killed livestock, and rendered entire neighbourhoods inaccessible. The most severely affected areas include Shagari Low-cost, Sabon Pegi, Modire, Yolde Pate, and Anguwan Tana. Poor drainage may have worsened the floods. Initial assessments by NEMA, Adamawa SEMA, and local partners indicate extensive destruction of homes, contamination of water sources, loss of food stocks, and damage to farmland at the peak of the planting season. Vulnerable groups, including women, children, older persons, and persons with disabilities, are disproportionately affected, with urgent needs for safe shelter, clean water, and food assistance. This project will deliver a coordinated, multi-sectoral emergency response over 45 days, reaching 10,000 individuals (1,667 households) in the worst-affected communities. Activities include: Unconditional cash transfers to enable affected households to meet immediate food needs and restore basic livelihoods. Distribution of emergency shelter kits and essential NFIs (mats, blankets, cooking sets). Provision of emergency WASH support through water purification tablets, hygiene kits, and community hygiene promotion and Protection (GBV and PSS)
